tools.name: get_setup_status
tools.description: Inspect the setup status of BillDog for this project. Returns an actionable checklist covering SDK keys, platform configuration, analytics ingestion, store credentials, products, entitlements, default offerings, and paywalls.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Get project metadata including bundle ID, package name, and registered domains.

tools.name: get_recent_sdk_activity
tools.description: Is the app sending data? For the last window_hours (default 24): events by name, purchases and session replays, split into sandbox and production, with has_traffic for each.

tools.name: resolve_placement_preview
tools.description: Dry-run preview of what a client SDK receives when resolving a placement. Returns the matched offering, packages, and assigned paywall.

tools.name: run_analytics_query
tools.description: Run a single analytics report. Returns a ReportResult envelope with columns + rows + optional totals. Available sources: events, revenue, cohorts, notifications, surveys, virtual_currency, subscriptions, paywalls, offerings, products, campaigns, experiments, journeys, customers. Available metrics: totals, timeseries, breakdown, funnel, retention, distribution, top_n, flow, compare, mrr_movement, ab_results, stickiness. Call discover_schema first if you need to know which (source, metric) pairings are supported. Reads production data unless sandbox is true; the result says which environment it read.

tools.name: discover_schema
tools.description: Return the full BillDog analytics schema — every (source, metric) pairing the project supports, with a 1-line description of what each returns. Call this once at the start of a session to know which combinations are valid.

tools.name: list_event_names
tools.description: List the event names this project received in the last `days` days (default 30), most frequent first, with each one's count and unique users. Useful when the user asks about an event by approximate name and you need the canonical one. Reads production data unless sandbox is true.

tools.name: list_cohorts
tools.description: List saved cohorts for this project. Each cohort has a definition (event-frequency / property / behavioral predicate) and a member_count. Pass a cohort id as the segment_id param to run_analytics_query to scope a report to that cohort.

tools.name: list_saved_views
tools.description: List saved analytics views for this project, each with what it asks (source, metric, dims, filters, date range, segment). Use get_saved_view_results to run one. Only views the user can see (shared with the project, or their own). pillar_id narrows to one area (revenue, product, surveys, …).

tools.name: get_saved_view_results
tools.description: Re-run a saved view and return its results. Equivalent to opening that report in the dashboard with the saved filters/range applied. Reads production data unless sandbox is true.

tools.name: list_products
tools.description: List all products configured in this project's catalog, including their identifiers, product types, subscription durations, and store mapping IDs.

tools.name: list_entitlements
tools.description: List all entitlements in this project and the product IDs associated with each entitlement.

tools.name: list_offerings
tools.description: List all offerings in this project, showing their packages, attached products, and default/current status.

tools.name: list_placements
tools.description: List all placements in this project, including access gating settings and linked offerings.

tools.name: apply_setup_plan
tools.description: Declaratively evaluate and execute a complete monetization catalog setup (products, entitlements, offerings, packages, placements). Defaults to dry_run: true for safe inspection of diffs and warnings before mutating. Set dry_run: false to commit.

tools.name: create_product
tools.description: Create a store product (subscription or in-app purchase) in the project catalog. A product can only be sold on a platform it has a store id for (app_store_product_id for Apple, play_store_product_id for Google, stripe_price_id for web); the result warns about any target platform missing one. If the identifier exists, nothing is changed (use update_product).

tools.name: update_product
tools.description: Update metadata, store IDs, or display pricing for an existing product in this project.

tools.name: create_entitlement
tools.description: Create a new entitlement in the catalog and optionally link it to products.

tools.name: update_entitlement
tools.description: Update display name, description, or linked products for an existing entitlement. product_ids REPLACES the list. On a live project, a change that removes a product (its buyers lose the entitlement) waits for an owner or admin to approve.

tools.name: set_entitlement_products
tools.description: Set the explicit list of product IDs granting an entitlement (replaces the list; only the links that change are touched). On a live project, removing a product (its buyers lose the entitlement) waits for an owner or admin to approve.

tools.name: create_offering
tools.description: Create a new offering with packages. Created inactive/non-current by default.

tools.name: manage_offering_packages
tools.description: Add or remove packages within an existing offering. A new package goes after the last one unless position is given. If customers can reach the offering (it is current, linked to a placement, or a published paywall uses it) and the project is live, the change waits for an owner or admin to approve it (awaiting_approval, with an approve_url to pass on). Live means a production purchase, or 10+ production customers, in the last 30 days; sample projects never count.

tools.name: set_current_offering
tools.description: Make an offering the project current offering (the others stop being current, atomically). On a live project (a production purchase, or 10+ production customers, in the last 30 days; sample projects never count) the change waits for an owner or admin to approve it: the result is awaiting_approval with an approve_url to pass on.

tools.name: create_placement
tools.description: Create a new placement in the project. Created unlinked by default.

tools.name: link_placement
tools.description: Link one or more offerings to a placement with priority order (replaces its links). On a live project (a production purchase, or 10+ production customers, in the last 30 days; sample projects never count) the change waits for an owner or admin to approve it: the result is awaiting_approval with an approve_url to pass on.

tools.name: list_paywalls
tools.description: List all paywalls in this project, including active state, wall type, and publication timestamps.

tools.name: get_paywall
tools.description: Get a paywall by UUID or identifier: status, layouts, offering, colours and copy_outline — every text and button with its component id, for update_paywall patch.copy. include_config returns the full draft and published configs (large).

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: List available paywall and onboarding templates from the BillDog template catalog.

tools.name: create_paywall_from_template
tools.description: Create a new paywall in the project from an existing template. Created as an inactive draft by default.

tools.name: design_paywall
tools.description: Design a paywall and save it as an inactive draft. Two ways: (1) pass `recipe`: you design it yourself — a compact layout (theme, presentation, body nodes such as text, icon, feature-list, products, button) that BillDog compiles into a native paywall. Its JSON schema is below; read the resource billdog://docs/paywall-recipe for the full language and design guidance. Uses no AI credit. If it does not compile, the error lists every problem; fix them and call again. (2) pass `prompt`: BillDog's AI designer (the same one as the dashboard's "Generate with AI") writes the recipe from your description and the project's offering and store listing. Uses one of the user's AI credits, charged only when a design compiles. Never write prices in text: the `products` node shows each package's real store price. Pass offering_id so the plan picker binds to that offering.

tools.name: update_paywall
tools.description: Apply constrained patch updates to a paywall's draft (copy, title, subtitle, CTA text, brand colors, offering binding). On a published paywall this edits the draft only: users keep seeing the published version until publish_paywall.

tools.name: preview_paywall
tools.description: Evaluate paywall publish gate (validating components, bindings, offerings) and generate a secure short-lived preview link and token.

tools.name: publish_paywall
tools.description: Publish a draft paywall to make it active for SDK delivery. Validates paywall before publishing. On a live project (a production purchase, or 10+ production customers, in the last 30 days; sample projects never count) the change waits for an owner or admin to approve it: the result is awaiting_approval with an approve_url to pass on. The approval publishes the draft as it was when you asked; edit it afterwards and you must ask again.

tools.name: unpublish_paywall
tools.description: Deactivate an active paywall. On a live project (a production purchase, or 10+ production customers, in the last 30 days; sample projects never count) the change waits for an owner or admin to approve it: the result is awaiting_approval with an approve_url to pass on.

tools.name: list_experiments
tools.description: List the project's experiments with their status, what devices are served now (variants, the shipped winner, or the control only), and each variant's paywall and traffic share.

tools.name: create_experiment
tools.description: Create a paywall A/B experiment as a DRAFT: each variant shows a different paywall at the same place in the app. The first variant is the control unless one says is_control. Traffic splits evenly unless every variant gives traffic_percent (they must add up to 100). It serves nothing until start_experiment, and every paywall in it must be published first.

tools.name: start_experiment
tools.description: Start (or resume) an experiment: users who reach its paywall are split between the variants. Refused unless it has 2+ variants whose traffic adds up to 100, exactly one control, every paywall published, and no other running experiment on the same paywall. On a live project (a production purchase, or 10+ production customers, in the last 30 days; sample projects never count) it waits for an owner or admin to approve it: the result is awaiting_approval with an approve_url to pass on.

tools.name: stop_experiment
tools.description: Stop an experiment. mode "pause" (default) and "end" both send every user back to the control paywall; a paused one can be started again, an ended one cannot. mode "ship_winner" ends it and serves winner_variant_id to everyone (its traffic becomes 100%, the others are retired). Live projects need approval as for start_experiment.

tools.name: get_experiment_results
tools.description: Per-variant results of an experiment for its whole run: users, conversions, conversion rate, revenue per user, lift vs control, p-value and significance (p < 0.05 with 100+ users per arm), plus a verdict: winner, loser, keep_running or no_data. Reads production unless sandbox is true.

tools.name: list_feature_flags
tools.description: List the project's feature flags: key, on/off, rollout percentage, variants, and whether it has release conditions (audience rules, edited in the dashboard).

tools.name: create_feature_flag
tools.description: Create a feature flag, OFF: every user gets false until update_feature_flag turns it on. The app reads it by key. For a multivariate flag give variants (2+, rollout_percentage adding up to 100, optional JSON payload each).

tools.name: update_feature_flag
tools.description: Turn a feature flag on (start) or off (stop), change its rollout percentage or variants, or rename it. Name it by flag_id or key. Turning it on needs a rollout_percentage above 0 (100 = everyone). A change to what users get, on a live project (a production purchase, or 10+ production customers, in the last 30 days), waits for an owner or admin to approve it: the result is awaiting_approval with an approve_url to pass on. Editing a flag that stays off applies at once.

tools.name: get_feature_flag_results
tools.description: How many users and evaluations got each value of a flag over the last N days (default 30, max 90), from the $feature_flag_called events the SDKs send. Name it by flag_id or key. Reads production unless sandbox is true.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List all BillDog projects accessible to the authenticated user, identifying the current active project, bundle ID, and platform.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create a new BillDog project for the authenticated user with a specified name, bundle ID, and platform. With the "Create projects" permission (Sign in with BillDog), this connection then works in the new project: every other tool acts on it, and use_project switches back. Otherwise the connection stays on its current project and the result says how to reconnect — do not configure the new project until then. Check result.connection.switched.

tools.name: create_public_sdk_key
tools.description: Generate a client-safe public SDK key (bd_public_live_... or bd_public_test_...) for mobile and web apps. Never mints secret keys.

tools.name: use_project
tools.description: Switch this connection to another project it may use: the project chosen when it was connected, or one it created with create_project. Every other tool then acts on that project. list_projects marks which ones this connection can use (connection_can_use).

tools.name: list_surveys
tools.description: List all multi-page surveys and micro-survey walls configured for this project.

tools.name: create_survey
tools.description: Save a survey as a DRAFT with its questions (activate it in the dashboard). Questions are checked as the dashboard checks them: a choice question needs choices, a rating needs maxRating ≥ 1, a link needs config.url.

tools.name: list_campaigns
tools.description: List all marketing and engagement campaigns configured for this project.

tools.name: create_campaign
tools.description: Save a campaign as a DRAFT. It reaches no one until it has an audience and is activated in the dashboard.

tools.name: list_journeys
tools.description: List all customer onboarding and engagement journeys with their sequence of steps.

tools.name: create_journey
tools.description: Save a linear journey as a DRAFT (activate it in the dashboard; branches are built on its canvas). entry_trigger.trigger is one of: signup, app_open, paywall_presented, paywall_dismissed, paywall_purchased, trial_start, trial_ending, subscription_created, subscription_renewed, subscription_cancelled, subscription_expired, billing_issue, survey_completed, inactivity, segment_entered, or custom_event with event_name.

tools.name: list_message_templates
tools.description: List the project's message templates (push, in-app, email, SMS) with their title and body, as the dashboard Templates library shows them. Deleted templates are excluded.

tools.name: create_message_template
tools.description: Save a reusable push or in-app message template (the same kind the dashboard Templates library shows). Use its id as template_id in a journey step.
